thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERS: High error rate + OOMs in us-west-2 serving cluster. Initial alert group: serving-runtime. Please acknowledge if oncall.

amanda: seeing spikes in pod restarts across rack-3 nodes — several containers exited with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION and OOM killed shortly after. metrics: pod-restarts ~ 45/m, tail latency p95-> 4.3s, error-rate -> 12%.

raj: logs look like RDMA retransmit bursts around the same time, retransmit counters jump. Could be packet loss causing KV cache inconsistencies and upstream backpressure. attaching quick logs: 
```
[2024-05-08T01:17:23Z] node-gpu-34 kernel: mlx5_core: ULP event: RDMA_ERR: retransmit=874 -> 1923
[2024-05-08T01:17:24Z] serving-agent: kvcache: mismatched_prefix -> evict cascade
[2024-05-08T01:17:24Z] runtime: gpu0: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION -> container exit
```

sre-liz: confirmed correlated: infra team reports link flaps on leaf-switch-12. This is multi-path, CVMP detected. Impact: distributed model shards lose quick KV lookup, runtime spins and allocs until OOM. Customer impact: a subset of heavy-serving customers (3 tenants) getting 5xx and long tails.

matt: initiating emergency mitigations: 1) route new traffic off affected rack to warm nodes, 2) enable degraded-serving fallback model (quantized) for customers on affected paths, 3) drain most unstable nodes. Starting now.

amanda: matt -> runbooks say use `rbx infra drain-node node-gpu-34 --grace 30` and set route tag: `route:set --cluster us-west-2 --policy degraded-fallback`. I'll run those.

matt: +1, deploy-bot please run fallback enable for tagged customers.

deploy-bot: Executing: `route:set --cluster us-west-2 --policy degraded-fallback` -> SUCCESS (12:18:05). Fallback model v1.4-q enabled for route group heavy-serving-1.

raj: while draining, we should disable KV cache warmups to avoid filler traffic. Suggest toggling kvcache.autofill=false on that node group.

amanda: ran drain on node-gpu-34 and node-gpu-35. k8s shows pods terminating, new pods scheduled on warm nodes in us-west-2-b. Observed immediate drop in retransmits after drain. latency p95 down to 1.1s.

sre-liz: infra folks are running switch-level diagnostics. They suspect a firmware bug that causes transient link-split under multipath. They've rolled back to previous fw on leaf-switch-12 and are monitoring.

matt: good. Next: collect core dumps from crashed containers, hold images, and open downstream RCA ticket. amanda can you collect `kubectl logs` and `gcore` outputs? Put artifacts in /tmp/incidents/1715009876.

amanda: collecting cores now, saving to s3://redwood-incidents/1715009876/. Also grabbed crash traces and dded out GPU stack traces.

raj: note for postmortem: add test that simulates intermittent RDMA retransmit bursts + KV cache churn to reproduce memory blowouts.

sre-liz: customer ops notified major tenants A, B with interim mitigation and ETA: degraded-serving active, no data leakage, estimated service restoration for normal path in 45m.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by matt. Escalation level: SEV2. Primary: matt, Secondary: tara.

matt: handing off to next oncall. tara, you're up for follow-on monitoring and teardown. Key next steps: 1) confirm fw rollback holds, 2) keep degraded-fallback until stable 1h, 3) validate no more CUDA crashes, 4) start RCA doc.

tara: acked. I'll take it from here, will post updates every 15m and close when we see 1h stability. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Handoff note: incident 1715009876 assigned to tara at 2024-05-08T02:25:00Z.

matt: leaving a small summary for PMs/SE: root cause likely RDMA path instability -> KV cache thrash -> runtime memory growth -> container OOMs. Mitigations applied: node drainage, routing to degraded quantized model, firmware rollback on leaf-switch-12. Postmortem owners: raj (infra repro), amanda (logs/artifacts), matt (incident).
